question: Why might a patient with high blood cell counts paradoxically face bleeding risks?

options.D: High blood pressure bursts skin capillaries

question: Which of these best describes a key clinical duty of an occupational health nurse?

options.A: Treating minor workplace injuries and managing chronic health checks
options.B: Designing factory buildings and heavy industrial machinery
options.C: Negotiating labor union contracts with company executives
options.D: Setting company stock prices and managing corporate budgets

explanation: As an occupational health nurse, you provide direct care by treating small injuries, giving first aid, and helping staff manage long-term health issues. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T4#GNS225_U7_T4_h6)

question: Which chemical substance is primarily responsible for causing uterine contractions and pain in dysmenorrhoea?

options.A: Insulin

options.D: Prostaglandins

question: Why must a nurse maintain neutrality when counseling patients about genetic risks?

options.B: To prevent patients from asking questions about their family

options.D: To ensure the hospital avoids paying for laboratory tests

question: What is a simple thing a nurse can do to build trust about injection safety?

options.A: Ask the doctor to perform all medication preparations
options.B: Show the sterile needle pack to the patient before opening it
options.C: Administer all injections behind a closed privacy curtain
options.D: Hide the syringe until the procedure is completely finished

question: Why should nurses care about the mental health of patients with visible skin problems?

options.A: Depression automatically cures the skin condition
options.B: Mental distress stops creams from absorbing
options.C: Psychological issues prevent any infections
options.D: Emotional stress can worsen physical skin flare-ups

question: How long should a patient typically fast before getting an FDG tracer injection for a PET scan?

options.D: 30 to 60 minutes

question: How do rapid diagnostic tests help in the fight against antibiotic resistance?

options.A: By increasing the potency of standard penicillin doses
options.B: By curing viral colds without needing any medication
options.C: By killing all resistant bacteria instantly on contact
options.D: By distinguishing viral infections from bacterial ones

explanation: Quick tests show if an illness is viral, stopping doctors from prescribing unnecessary antibiotics (since antibiotics don't touch viruses!). [learn more](GNS313_U1_T18#GNS313_U1_T18_h6)

question: Which of these is an example of non-pharmacological (drug-free) pain relief?

options.A: Applying a warm compress to a sore muscle
options.B: Administering a prescribed dose of oral ibuprofen
options.C: Dispensing a scheduled narcotic pain pill
options.D: Injecting intravenous morphine into the patient port

explanation: You got it! Warm compresses, massage, and changing positions help ease pain without using drugs (pharmaceuticals). [learn more](GNS123_U2_T1#GNS123_U2_T1_h4)

question: What does pharmacokinetics mean?

options.A: What the body does to the drug over time
options.B: How chemical structures are built in a laboratory
options.C: What the drug does to change cellular function
options.D: How nurses calculate pediatric dosages safely

explanation: Think of pharmacokinetics as your body's journey with the drug—absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T2#GNS125_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why is severe pain a major barrier when you are trying to talk with a patient?

options.A: Pain prevents the nurse from hearing any non-verbal body language.
options.B: Pain automatically changes the native language spoken by the patient.
options.C: The patient's focus is entirely consumed by managing physical discomfort.
options.D: It turns a normal social conversation into a formal medical emergency.

explanation: Spot on! When someone is hurting badly, all their energy goes into surviving the pain, making it hard to concentrate on a conversation. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h5)

question: During which stage of pregnancy do the structures that form the fallopian tubes grow and fuse?

options.A: Near the end of the second trimester
options.B: During the first trimester
options.C: Throughout the third trimester
options.D: After birth during infancy

question: When using a bulb syringe to clear a newborn's airway, which part should you suction first?

options.A: Mouth
options.B: Pharynx
options.C: Trachea
options.D: Nose

explanation: Always suction the mouth before the nose! If you do the nose first, the baby might gasp and accidentally inhale any fluid sitting in their mouth. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h2)

question: Why might a nurse researcher choose the median instead of the mean when looking at how long patients stayed in the hospital?

options.A: The median is always a lower number than the mean
options.B: A few patients staying very long periods can pull the mean upward
options.C: Hospital administrators legally require the use of medians
options.D: The mean cannot be calculated using days as a unit

explanation: Exactly! If a couple of patients had unusually long stays, they would skew the average (mean) way up. The median sits right in the middle and isn't easily tricked by those extreme cases. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T2#GNS217_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is a very common early sign that patients with developing disseminated sclerosis report?

options.A: Complete paralysis of both legs
options.B: Vision changes like optic neuritis
options.C: Severe high blood pressure
options.D: Total loss of long-term memory

explanation: Keep an eye out for this: inflammation of the optic nerve causing blurry vision or eye pain is frequently one of the very first warning signs of MS. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is the medical term for heavy, prolonged menstrual bleeding, which is very common in women with fibroids?

options.A: Metrorrhagia
options.B: Dysmenorrhea
options.C: Amenorrhea
options.D: Menorrhagia

explanation: That's right! Menorrhagia simply means abnormally heavy or long periods. (Remember: 'rrhagia' sounds like rushing heavy flow!). [learn more](GNS216_U5_T19#GNS216_U5_T19_h3)

question: How long should children wash their hands with soap to properly get rid of germs?

options.A: Twenty seconds
options.B: Ten seconds
options.C: One hour
options.D: Two minutes

explanation: Twenty seconds is the magic number! Singing a short song helps kids scrub long enough to break down the germs on their skin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h5)

question: What are the three main pillars that make up evidence-based practice?

options.A: Patient age, family background, and disease diagnosis
options.B: Research evidence, clinical expertise, and patient values
options.C: Hospital policy, physician orders, and insurance budgets
options.D: Textbook theory, nursing tradition, and administrative rules

explanation: EBP is a balanced approach that requires combining valid research findings with the nurse's professional judgment and what matters to the patient. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is an important task for school management when evaluating their health programme?

options.A: Reviewing clinic attendance logs to spot health trends
options.B: Changing the academic grading system every term
options.C: Firing teachers who report sick with malaria
options.D: Keeping all student medical records strictly secret from staff

explanation: Exactly! Checking clinic records helps leaders spot recurring health issues early and take quick, smart action. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h7)

question: What is the main job of mineralocorticoids in the human body?

options.A: Regulating sodium and fluid balance
options.B: Suppressing white blood cell activity
options.C: Increasing protein synthesis in muscles
options.D: Lowering high blood sugar levels

explanation: Mineralocorticoids (like aldosterone) work on the kidneys to manage salt (sodium) and water in your body. It's all about keeping your fluid balance steady! [learn more](GNS223_U7_T4#GNS223_U7_T4_h2)

question: How do non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) help relieve pain?

options.A: Blocking prostaglandins to reduce pain and swelling
options.B: Destroying bacteria directly in the bloodstream
options.C: Permanently stopping all white blood cell production
options.D: Freezing the skin to numb local nerve endings

explanation: You nailed it! NSAIDs stop the body from making prostaglandins, which are the chemical messengers of pain and swelling. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h7)

question: A patient is anxious and has a rapid heart rate before surgery. Which nursing action is best to help calm them?

options.A: Advise the patient to ignore the upcoming surgery entirely
options.B: Leave the patient alone in a brightly lit room to rest
options.C: Guide the patient through slow deep breathing exercises
options.D: Encourage the patient to drink several cups of strong coffee

explanation: Taking slow, deep breaths is a simple, powerful way to quiet the fight-or-flight response, slow down a racing heart, and ease pre-surgery nerves. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T8#GNS123_U1_T8_h7)

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the ABCDE systematic assessment approach?

options.A: Bedside
options.B: Breathing
options.C: Blood pressure
options.D: Bleeding

explanation: In the ABCDE emergency assessment framework, B stands for evaluating the patient's breathing status and chest movement. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h2)

question: Which animal is the primary natural reservoir and transmitter of Lassa virus to humans?

options.A: Migratory birds
options.B: Multimammate rats
options.C: Freshwater fish
options.D: Domesticated dogs

explanation: The multimammate rat sheds the Lassa virus in its urine and droppings, which can contaminate human food and living areas. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h3)

question: During which phase of cancer development do cells gain aggressive traits and learn to spread?

options.A: Progression
options.B: Initiation
options.C: Promotion
options.D: Encapsulation

explanation: Progression is the final, full-speed-ahead phase where the cells become truly malignant and start invading. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T7#GNS321_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the main goal of a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP)?

options.A: To calculate the annual salary bonus for senior head nurses
options.B: To outline specific steps and support to correct performance deficiencies
options.C: To immediately terminate a nurse without a review process
options.D: To change the hospital's clinical nursing policies for all staff

explanation: A PIP is a helpful coaching tool, not a sack letter. It sets clear, achievable steps and gives you support to master any weak areas. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h6)

question: A pregnant patient complains of severe lower back ache after standing for hours at her market stall. What is the main cause?

options.A: Inflammation of the bone marrow inside the vertebrae
options.B: Early degeneration of the spinal discs from calcium loss
options.C: Direct pressure of the fetal head on the lumbar nerves
options.D: Fatigue of the lower back muscles due to exaggerated spinal curves

explanation: The muscles along the lower spine have to work overtime to keep the body upright against the forward pull of pregnancy, leading to tiredness and aches. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h3)

question: Why is coaching the patient to take deep breaths so important during an unsedated sigmoidoscopy?

options.A: It helps relax their belly and pelvic muscles, making it easier to pass the scope.
options.B: It removes the need for lubrication.
options.C: It keeps their blood pressure artificially high.
options.D: It keeps them from swallowing air into their lungs.

explanation: Spot on! When cramps hit, patients naturally tense up. Deep breathing helps them relax those muscles so the procedure goes smoother. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T6#GNS221_U2_T6_h5)

question: What is a major cause of accidental needlestick injuries during injections?

options.A: Pulling the skin for Z-track
options.B: Using the ventrogluteal site
options.C: Selecting a 25-gauge needle
options.D: Recapping used needles

question: Why do leprosy patients often end up with serious sores on their hands and feet?

options.A: Unbearable itching makes them scratch too hard
options.B: Blood completely stops flowing to the fingers and toes
options.C: Loss of feeling causes them to injure themselves without knowing
options.D: Bacteria directly dissolve the skin cells

explanation: Because they can't feel pain, heat, or sharp objects, minor cuts go unnoticed and turn into nasty ulcers. You're building solid clinical instincts! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is the 'harm reduction myth' regarding medicalised FGM?

options.C: The belief that clinical FGM is safer and causes fewer complications

question: Why is sharing a real local story often better than using a bunch of statistics?

options.A: Local people cannot understand mathematical percentages at all
options.B: Stories are more memorable and humanize the issue for the audience
options.C: Statistics are illegal to share in community health meetings
options.D: Stories guarantee that government funding will be approved immediately

explanation: Numbers are helpful, but human stories touch the heart and make people truly feel why an issue matters. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T8#GNS124_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is an absolute must-have medication every midwife must carry for the third stage of labor?

options.A: Intravenous general anesthesia
options.B: Magnesium sulfate for chronic cough
options.C: Oxytocin for hemorrhage prevention
options.D: Broad-spectrum oral antibiotics

question: Why must care homes undergo regular government inspections?

options.A: To determine the weekly menu options for the dining hall
options.B: To collect annual property taxes directly from the facility owners
options.C: To ensure compliance with safety, sanitation, and quality standards
options.D: To recruit nursing students for government hospital positions

explanation: You nailed it! Regular checks make sure facilities keep up high standards of cleanliness, safety, and patient care. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T12#GNS324_U5_T12_h3)

question: Which behavior is a classic example of an automatism during a psychomotor seizure?

options.A: Sudden falling backward with stiffened limbs

options.C: Sustained rhythmic shaking of both lower limbs
options.D: Complete unresponsiveness with rigid posturing

question: Under current Nigerian laws, when is a pregnancy termination generally allowed?

options.A: If the pregnancy results from consensual teenage dating
options.B: To save the life of the pregnant woman
options.C: In all cases during the first trimester
options.D: Whenever the woman requests it in writing

explanation: Spot on. Nigerian laws are quite strict and typically permit abortion only when carrying the pregnancy to term puts the mother's life in danger. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T019#GNS226_U5_T019_h6)

question: In many Nigerian clinical settings, what is a major hurdle that stops patients from getting their prescribed drugs?

options.A: An oversupply of specialized surgical instruments
options.B: Out-of-pocket spending by patients
options.C: Excessive availability of free hospital parking
options.D: Mandatory international travel for simple prescriptions

explanation: When patients have to pay cash directly for every drug without health insurance, buying medications becomes a serious daily struggle. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h6)

question: Which fluid fills the large cavity behind the lens to keep the retina in place?

question: Why do theatres carefully monitor room temperature and humidity during surgery?

options.A: To make the room comfortable for visitors and family members

options.C: To discourage bacterial growth and prevent patient hypothermia

explanation: Controlling the climate stops bacteria from multiplying and protects the patient's body heat while they are under anesthesia. You've got this! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h1)

question: During a physical assessment of a patient with second-week enteric fever, which organs are you most likely to find enlarged?

options.A: Liver and spleen
options.B: Adrenal glands
options.C: Thyroid and parathyroid
options.D: Kidneys and pancreas

explanation: You nailed it! The bacteria loves to hide and multiply in the body's filtering tissues, leading to a swollen liver and spleen (hepatosplenomegaly). [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h3)

question: What is the very first thing you should do before putting any topical medication on a patient's skin?

options.A: Massage the skin vigorously to increase blood flow
options.B: Apply a thick layer of petroleum jelly to protect surrounding tissue
options.C: Warm the cream under hot running water
options.D: Assess the condition and integrity of the target skin area

question: A family is hesitant to discuss a terminal diagnosis with their elderly parent due to cultural traditions. As a nurse, what is your best first step?

options.A: Explore the family's cultural concerns and work collaboratively to honor their values while ensuring patient comfort
options.B: Report the family to hospital security for withholding medical information
options.C: Ignore the family and tell the patient the diagnosis immediately without warning
options.D: Discontinue all palliative support until the family changes their tradition

explanation: Great nursing requires teamwork with the family! By listening to their cultural perspectives, you can find a respectful way forward that keeps the patient comfortable and honored. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h8)

question: Where does most of the money for federal teaching hospitals come from?

options.A: Federal government budgetary allocations
options.B: Community development association levies
options.C: Local government monthly revenue shares
options.D: Voluntary donations from religious bodies

explanation: You nailed it! Teaching hospitals are big federal projects, so they rely heavily on the national budget to keep running. [learn more](GST322_U5_T4#GST322_U5_T4_h4)

question: What is the correct technique for pulling out a peripheral IV catheter?

options.A: Twist the hub rapidly while pulling outward with force

options.C: Flush the line with saline right before pulling it out
options.D: Pull it out smoothly and parallel to the skin surface

question: How does team nursing differ from total patient care?

options.A: Total patient care involves no registered nurses at all
options.B: Total patient care is only used in surgical operating theatres
options.C: Team nursing uses a mix of different staff cadres to care for a group of patients
options.D: Team nursing requires one registered nurse to do everything alone

explanation: Well done! Total patient care means one nurse handles everything for a patient, while team nursing shares the workload among a group of mixed staff. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why is family planning counseling important early in the postpartum period?

options.A: Traditional birth control methods never work after childbirth
options.B: Women cannot get pregnant while breastfeeding
options.C: Ovulation can happen before her monthly period returns
options.D: Hormonal contraceptives must start on delivery day

explanation: Many women are surprised to learn they can release an egg and get pregnant again before they even see their first postpartum period! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h7)

question: Why do red blood cells end up leaking into the urine when someone has Acute Glomerulonephritis?

options.A: Severe infection inside the urinary meatus
options.B: Rapid breakdown of muscular tissue in the legs
options.C: Direct physical trauma to the external bladder lining
options.D: The damaged filtering membrane becomes too porous

question: What makes a competitive antagonist unique?

options.A: It destroys the agonist molecules inside the bloodstream
options.B: It binds to a completely different site on the cell
options.C: It fights with the agonist for the same receptor site
options.D: It changes the chemical structure of the target organ

explanation: Competitive means they are wrestling for the exact same parking spot (receptor site)! Whoever gets there first or has more numbers wins the spot. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T7#GNS125_U5_T7_h2)

question: What does the acronym BLS stand for in nursing and emergency care?

options.A: Breathing Lung System
options.B: Body Life Stimulation
options.C: Basic Life Support
options.D: Basic Lung Safety

explanation: BLS stands for Basic Life Support, which covers emergency measures like CPR and AED use. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T6#GNS321_U2_T6_h1)

question: When is it strictly necessary for a nurse to use soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

options.A: Only when starting a surgical procedure in the theater
options.B: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids
options.C: Whenever the alcohol dispenser is empty for the day
options.D: Every time a nurse enters a new hospital ward

explanation: Alcohol rubs cannot remove physical dirt or certain tough bacterial spores as effectively as physical washing with soap and water. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h3)

question: Why does Graves' disease cause hyperthyroidism?

options.A: The pituitary gland stops releasing any regulatory hormones
options.B: Dietary iodine levels become excessively high in the bloodstream
options.C: Thyroid tissue undergoes widespread autoimmune destruction
options.D: Antibodies mimic TSH and continuously stimulate the thyroid gland

explanation: In Graves' disease, rogue antibodies trick the thyroid by acting just like TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone), forcing the gland to pump out way too much thyroid hormone. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T13#GNS222_U2_T13_h5)

question: Why does keeping a young married girl away from her friends and family hurt her mental health so much?

options.A: It forces her to make independent financial decisions
options.B: It cuts off her normal support system of friends and family
options.C: It provides her with too much free time to worry
options.D: It eliminates all contact with healthcare workers

explanation: Taking a child away from school and peers destroys her support network, leaving her all alone to handle adult stress. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T9#GNS312_U1_T9_h5)

question: What exactly is a hospital-acquired complication?

options.A: An expected outcome of chronic disease progression
options.B: A negative health event developing during hospital care
options.C: An illness the patient had before admission
options.D: A normal side effect of curative surgery

explanation: You've got this! These are issues that pop up because a patient is in the healthcare setting or undergoing treatment, rather than being there when they first arrived. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T11#GNS123_U5_T11_h1)

question: A patient on chemotherapy has a very low white blood cell count. What should be your top nursing priority?

options.A: Administering high doses of oral iron supplements
options.B: Encouraging heavy physical exercise to combat fatigue
options.C: Preparing the patient for immediate surgical tumor removal
options.D: Protecting the patient from potential sources of infection

explanation: Brilliant nursing logic! White blood cells are our body's soldiers. When their count drops (neutropenia), our main job is to guard the patient fiercely against any germs and infections. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T6#GNS321_U1_T6_h6)

question: What happens to the body's normal breakdown pathways during a severe drug overdose?

options.A: They become completely saturated
options.B: They speed up to eliminate the drug instantly
options.C: They convert the drug into harmless vitamins
options.D: They shut down permanently within seconds

explanation: Think of it like a traffic jam: there is simply too much drug for the body's processing enzymes to handle all at once, so the pathways get completely overwhelmed. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T9#GNS125_U2_T9_h3)

question: Which of these common germs needs to hijack a living host cell in order to multiply?

options.A: Virus
options.B: Fungus
options.C: Bacterium
options.D: Parasite

explanation: Think of viruses as tiny freeloaders! They don't have the tools to reproduce on their own, so they must break into a living host cell to multiply. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T2#GNS313_U1_T2_h2)

question: How often should a bedbound patient ideally be repositioned to prevent pressure injuries?

options.A: Only when the patient complains
options.B: Once every twelve hours
options.C: At least every two hours
options.D: Once per day during the morning shift

question: Why should you avoid using cold compresses to treat pain during a sickle cell crisis?

options.A: Refrigerated items increase the risk of skin breakdown over swollen joints
options.B: Cold temperatures cause blood vessels to constrict and promote further sickling
options.C: Low temperatures stop intravenous pain medications from working properly

question: In some traditional Nigerian settings, how might hiring a paid home care nurse be viewed by the community?

options.B: As a mandatory legal requirement for all households
options.C: As a government-sponsored welfare program
options.D: As a sign of abandoning family care duties

explanation: You got it! Culturally, people sometimes wrongly assume hiring a nurse means you are neglecting your sick family member. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T9#GNS324_U1_T9_h5)

question: A nurse is about to give a vesicant chemo drug through a hand vein. What is the most crucial check before starting?

options.A: Instructing the patient to tightly flex their arm muscles throughout the entire infusion
options.B: Warming the intravenous fluid bag to body temperature to prevent vein spasms
options.C: Verifying brisk blood return to confirm the catheter is properly placed inside the vein
options.D: Diluting the concentrated medication with sterile water instead of normal saline

question: Why is working alongside local traditional and religious leaders vital when trying to stop harmful practices?

options.A: Staff members get spread too thin and miss targets.
options.B: Every objective gets achieved much faster.
options.C: Employees experience a sharp decrease in stress.
options.D: Patient satisfaction scores automatically double.

explanation: Trying to do everything at once usually means nothing gets done well. It's always better to focus on a few key priorities! [learn more](GST321_U2_T1#GST321_U2_T1_h6)

question: What blood product is typically given to replace lost oxygen-carrying capacity in a massive haemorrhage?

options.A: Normal saline solution
options.B: Albumin protein liquid
options.C: Pure platelet concentrate
options.D: Packed red blood cells

explanation: Packed red blood cells specifically restore the hemoglobin and red blood cells needed to carry oxygen to tissues. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h7)

question: Which patient finding means you need to call for emergency help right away?

options.A: A heart rate of 102 beats per minute while walking
options.B: Blood pressure of 70/40 mmHg with altered mental status
options.C: Mild fatigue at the end of a normal daily work shift
options.D: Occasional fluttering sensations in the chest while resting

explanation: When blood pressure drops that low and the patient is confused, the bad rhythm is starving the brain and body of blood flow. That's an all-hands-on-deck emergency! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h6)

question: A new mother looks pale, feels dizzy, and her pad is soaked with bright red blood within 20 minutes. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Assess the uterine fundus for tone and massage if boggy
options.B: Wait until the scheduled six-week postnatal checkup
options.C: Tell the mother to walk around the room to improve circulation
options.D: Encourage the mother to drink large volumes of cold water

explanation: Great clinical thinking! These are classic signs of postpartum hemorrhage. Checking and massaging the uterus helps it contract and stops the bleeding. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h3)

question: A patient is admitted with suspected celiac disease. Which specific blood test does the nurse expect the healthcare provider to order first?

options.A: Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA)
options.B: Serum amylase and lipase levels
options.C: Anti-tissue transglutaminase (tTG) antibodies
options.D: Blood urea nitrogen and creatinine

explanation: Serologic antibody testing for anti-tTG is the standard primary screening tool used to detect celiac disease in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h6)

question: What is the primary function of the dorsal root ganglion?

options.A: It generates motor commands for reflex actions
options.B: It connects the spinal nerve directly to the sympathetic trunk
options.C: It produces cerebrospinal fluid to cushion the nerve
options.D: It houses the cell bodies of sensory neurons

explanation: The dorsal root ganglion is a distinct swelling along the sensory root that contains the cell bodies of incoming sensory neurons. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of having good sanitation facilities?

options.A: Safe disposal of human waste
options.B: Production of clean drinking water
options.C: Elimination of flying insect pests
options.D: Reduction of indoor air pollution

explanation: Great job! Sanitation is all about making sure human waste is handled safely so it doesn't contaminate our environment or spread disease. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h2)

question: How does tubular secretion differ fundamentally from tubular reabsorption?

options.A: Secretion eliminates useful nutrients, while reabsorption removes metabolic poisons
options.B: Secretion occurs only in the renal cortex, while reabsorption occurs only in the medulla
options.C: Secretion moves substances from blood into the tubule, while reabsorption moves them back to the blood
options.D: Secretion uses passive transport only, while reabsorption requires high blood pressure

explanation: Secretion adds materials to the forming urine from the capillaries, whereas reabsorption rescues valuable substances from the filtrate. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the main goal of chemoprophylaxis?

options.A: To prevent an infection before it develops or turns active
options.B: To cure a chronic autoimmune disease permanently
options.C: To destroy normal healthy flora in the gut
options.D: To replace surgical hand hygiene in hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Chemoprophylaxis is just a medical term for using medications to stop an infection before it even starts. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T11#GNS313_U2_T11_h5)

question: Why can a needle look perfectly clean yet still carry a dangerous virus?

options.A: Microscopic traces of infected blood remain inside the hollow bore
options.B: Skin bacteria react with the metal to create new pathogens
options.C: The virus travels through the air surrounding the needle
options.D: Plastic needles absorb viruses and release them later

explanation: Even if you can't see it, an invisible film of fluid inside a needle hub holds enough viral particles to cause a new infection. That's why we never reuse needles! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h2)

question: Your catheterized patient has had no urine output for two hours and feels lower belly discomfort. What do you check first?

options.A: Check the tubing for kinks, twists, or compression under the patient
options.B: Call the doctor to report acute kidney failure
options.C: Remove the catheter immediately and insert a new one
options.D: Inject sterile water into the balloon to secure it further

explanation: Always look for the simple fix first! A twisted or flattened tube is usually the culprit when urine suddenly stops flowing. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T21#GNS212_U1_T21_h8)

question: What is the main job of the ascending nerve tracts passing through the brain stem?

options.A: Coordinating balance with the cerebellum
options.B: Carrying sensory signals up to the brain
options.C: Producing automatic breathing rhythms
options.D: Transmitting motor orders down to muscles

explanation: Remember that 'ascending' means going up! These tracts carry sensory information from your body all the way up to higher brain areas. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h3)

question: When doing a quick physical check, which sign helps you spot possible anaemia?

options.A: Swelling of the lower legs
options.B: Pallor of the conjunctiva
options.C: Yellowing of the sclera
options.D: Redness of the palms

explanation: Easy and quick! Pulling down the lower eyelid lets you check the conjunctiva. If it looks pale instead of nice and pink, it's a quick clinical clue that the blood count might be low. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T020#GNS226_U2_T020_h4)

question: Which patient sign means you should grab and attach an AED right away?

options.A: Severe chest pain and heavy sweating
options.B: Confusion and mild shortness of breath
options.C: High fever and a rapid pulse rate
options.D: Unresponsiveness and no normal breathing

explanation: An AED is meant for sudden cardiac arrest. We look for someone who has collapsed, doesn't respond, and isn't breathing normally. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which of these heart rhythms needs an immediate emergency shock?

options.A: Sinus Bradycardia
options.B: Ventricular Fibrillation
options.C: Asystole
options.D: Pulseless Electrical Activity

explanation: Ventricular Fibrillation (VF) is a shockable rhythm because the heart still has wild electrical activity that a shock can clear. Flatlines (asystole) need chest compressions and meds, not shocks! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T17#GNS213_U1_T17_h1)

question: Which behavior from a nurse will immediately make a teenager shut down and stop talking?

options.A: Listening actively to the patient's concerns
options.B: Maintaining a calm and welcoming facial expression
options.C: Asking simple open-ended questions
options.D: Displaying a judgmental or scolding attitude

explanation: Spot on! Scolding or moralizing makes teens feel ashamed, leading them to hide important health information and avoid future visits. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T17#GNS312_U3_T17_h6)

question: How does palliative care view the dying process?

options.A: As an emergency requiring immediate surgery
options.B: As a normal part of the human life cycle
options.C: As a medical failure that must be avoided
options.D: As a punishment for past life actions

explanation: Palliative care respects life's natural journey. It doesn't rush death, nor does it try to unnaturally drag it out—it accepts it as a normal part of living. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T2#GNS321_U4_T2_h2)

question: How does evaluation differ from monitoring in a community health program?

options.A: Evaluation is optional, whereas monitoring is required by international law
options.B: Evaluation focuses entirely on staff discipline, while monitoring deals with drug supplies
options.C: Evaluation assesses the final outcomes and impact, while monitoring tracks ongoing daily activities
options.D: Evaluation is done before any data is collected, while monitoring happens only at the end

explanation: Spot on! Monitoring checks the process as it happens day-to-day, while evaluation measures the final results and overall success of the project. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h8)

question: A nurse notices that an elderly patient living alone has dim lighting and loose rugs. What action best mitigates this risk?

options.A: Telling the patient to stop walking around the house entirely
options.B: Immediately transferring the patient to a nursing home facility
options.C: Conducting a safety assessment and arranging to clear hazards with the family
options.D: Waiting until the next scheduled annual medical checkup

explanation: Identifying hazards early and working with support networks to fix them prevents accidental falls at home. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h8)

question: Which symptom should a recovering patient at home report to their healthcare team right away?

options.A: Slow improvement in overall daily stamina
options.B: New numbness or tingling in the affected limb
options.C: Mild muscle soreness the day after exercise
options.D: Needing extra rest periods during afternoon chores

explanation: You nailed it! Numbness or tingling can mean a nerve is being squished or blood flow is blocked, so it needs a quick check. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h8)

question: Why does a patient with osteoarthritis usually feel pain in their joint?

options.A: Rapid overproduction of calcium and vitamin D in the blood
options.B: Loss of articular cartilage exposing subchondral bone
options.C: Sudden calcification of the major surrounding ligaments
options.D: Systemic autoimmune attack on the synovial membrane

explanation: When the protective cushion (cartilage) wears away, bone starts rubbing directly against bone. Ouch! That causes the friction and pain. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T20#GNS222_U1_T20_h2)

question: Why is a chest X-ray usually done right after a thoracentesis?

options.A: To measure the exact volume of remaining chest fluid
options.B: To check if the rib bones healed from the puncture
options.C: To confirm lung expansion and check for a collapsed lung
options.D: To verify that the heart valves are working normally

explanation: Spot on! An X-ray lets us double-check that the lung expanded nicely and that no air slipped into the chest cavity. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T17#GNS213_U2_T17_h5)

question: A patient keeps a 5-day food diary on the ward, but the nurse notices the meals look unusually tiny. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: Weighed food records are completely useless in hospital settings
options.B: The patient is secretly eating large amounts of hidden snacks
options.C: The patient may be altering intake or underreporting to simplify logging
options.D: The patient's metabolic rate has suddenly dropped to zero

explanation: Exactly. Writing down every little thing can be tiring, so patients sometimes eat less or forget to log certain items! [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h4)

question: What happens right after a hormone hooks up with its target receptor?

options.A: A cascade of chemical messages is triggered inside the cell
options.B: The hormone is destroyed by the circulating antibodies
options.C: The cell membrane seals completely shut to block other signals
options.D: The cell immediately undergoes programmed cell death

explanation: Think of it like ringing a doorbell: once the hormone binds, it sets off an internal chain reaction that changes how the cell behaves and does its job. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T11#GNS211_U1_T11_h1)

question: What does population health nursing primarily focus on?

options.A: The financial balance sheet of a health clinic
options.B: The health outcomes of an entire group of people
options.C: The surgical procedures performed in a single hospital ward
options.D: The genetic profile of an individual patient

explanation: Population health looks beyond the individual patient to protect and promote the well-being of whole communities. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h1)

question: What is the main way we define gender-based violence (GBV)?

options.A: Harmful acts based on sex or gender identity
options.B: Violent crimes committed exclusively against adult males
options.C: Accidental domestic injuries occurring at home
options.D: Physical injuries sustained during a street fight

explanation: GBV happens because of a person's sex or gender roles, rather than just random bad luck or street crime. You've got this! [learn more](GNS312_U4_T13#GNS312_U4_T13_h1)

question: A nurse researcher wants to check if there is a link between water source type and the prevalence of cholera in a community. Which study type is best?

options.A: Qualitative interview study
options.B: Analytical cross-sectional study
options.C: Purely descriptive case report
options.D: Longitudinal clinical trial

explanation: When you are looking for a connection between two things at one specific time, an analytical cross-sectional study is your best friend. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h3)

question: What position is the patient usually placed in during a sigmoidoscopy?

options.A: Left lateral (Sims') position
options.B: Flat on their back (supine)
options.C: Sitting upright in a high chair
options.D: Flat on their stomach (prone)

explanation: You got it! Lying on the left side (Sims' position) naturally aligns the lower bowel, making the scope easier and safer to insert. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T6#GNS221_U2_T6_h5)

question: You check a patient's vital signs before giving their scheduled beta-blocker. Which finding means you should hold the dose and check with the doctor?

options.A: Mild swelling in the lower ankles by evening
options.B: A resting heart rate of 50 beats per minute
options.C: A blood pressure reading of 120 over 80 mmHg
options.D: A slight complaint of daytime feeling sleepy

explanation: Beta-blockers slow the heart down. If the pulse drops below 60 beats per minute, that's bradycardia, and giving another dose could cause it to drop too low! [learn more](GNS223_U1_T4#GNS223_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why do endocrine problems usually cause a full-body crisis instead of just a local issue?

options.A: Hormones only work when the patient is under severe stress
options.B: Endocrine organs are all connected directly to the brain
options.C: Hormones travel through the bloodstream to affect many organs
options.D: Endocrine glands store large amounts of toxic waste products

explanation: Think of hormones like mail carriers circulating through the blood vessels. Because they travel everywhere, trouble in just one gland can quickly shake up multiple body systems at once! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T16#GNS222_U2_T16_h1)

question: How do health orderlies help control infections in the theatre?

options.A: They wear sterile gowns and handle surgical instruments
options.B: They scrub the surgeon's hands before the operation begins
options.C: They help clean the theatre and dispose of waste between cases
options.D: They sterilize surgical blades inside the autoclave machine

explanation: By clearing waste and cleaning up after procedures, orderlies play a huge part in keeping the theatre safe from hospital-acquired infections. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h6)

question: Which type of food hazard includes cleaning chemicals and leftover pesticide sprays?

options.A: Physical hazards
options.B: Biological hazards
options.C: Nutritional hazards
options.D: Chemical hazards

explanation: You guessed it—chemical hazards involve toxic substances like cleaning agents and farm chemicals that accidentally get into our food supply. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h1)

question: Why is letting the chest spring all the way back up between compressions so important during CPR?

options.A: It gives the rescuer time to rest their arms
options.B: It lowers the child's body temperature
options.C: It prevents the ribs from fracturing
options.D: It allows blood to refill the heart chambers

explanation: Think of the heart like a sponge. When you push down, you squeeze blood out; when you let the chest recoil, it refills with fresh blood for the next push! [learn more](GNS212_U2_T3#GNS212_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which food group is most helpful to prevent constipation in older adults who aren't very active?

options.A: Simple sugars
options.B: Animal proteins
options.C: Dietary fiber
options.D: Saturated fats

explanation: Great thinking! Fiber adds bulk to stool and keeps things moving smoothly, helping make up for slower digestion in older age. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T4#GNS321_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which agency is responsible for regulating food and drugs in Nigeria?

options.A: NAFDAC
options.B: Standard Organisation of Nigeria
options.C: National Youth Service Corps
options.D: Federal Ministry of Education

explanation: You've got this! NAFDAC is our watchdog, keeping watch over how drugs are made, imported, and sold across Nigeria. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h2)

question: How often should essential emergency equipment like crash carts be checked on a hospital ward?

options.A: Every shift
options.B: Once a month
options.C: Only after a patient codes
options.D: Once a year

explanation: Routine shift checks ensure that emergency items are present, functional, and ready for immediate use. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h6)

question: Which meningeal layer wraps around the brain so tightly that it dips into every single groove and fold?

options.A: Dura mater
options.B: Arachnoid mater
options.C: Periosteal layer
options.D: Pia mater

explanation: You got it! The pia mater is soft and tender, clinging closely to every curve of the brain like a second skin. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T8#GNS211_U3_T8_h4)

question: When is an autocratic leadership style most appropriate in a primary health care setting?

options.A: During a routine community health education meeting
options.B: During a sudden medical emergency or trauma resuscitation
options.C: When scheduling the monthly staff social gathering
options.D: When designing a new long-term clinic budget

explanation: Quick, direct orders without debate are essential in urgent medical emergencies to save time and prevent errors. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h3)

question: A nurse is preparing to start a blood transfusion for an adult patient. Which intravenous solution should be used to prime the Y-tubing?

options.A: 5% dextrose in water
options.B: 0.45% sodium chloride
options.C: 0.9% sodium chloride
options.D: Lactated Ringer's solution

explanation: Normal saline (0.9% sodium chloride) is isotonic and compatible with red blood cells, preventing hemolysis that other solutions might cause. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T8#GNS123_U2_T8_h6)

question: A nurse wants to test a new handwashing style on two hospital wards without disrupting how the wards are already set up. What is the best study type?

options.A: Retrospective case-control study
options.B: Cross-sectional survey
options.C: Quasi-experimental study
options.D: Randomized controlled trial

explanation: Correct! When you can't randomly mix up individual patients because of real-world ward setups, a quasi-experimental design saves the day. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T13#GNS217_U3_T13_h4)

question: A family caregiver is overwhelmed because their relative with memory loss keeps missing doses and mixing up pill times. What is the most helpful nursing intervention?

options.A: Tell the caregiver to stop giving all medications immediately
options.B: Warn them that missing doses has zero effect on chronic illnesses
options.C: Advise them to let the patient manage everything independently
options.D: Suggest practical tools like a labeled pill organizer and a daily schedule

explanation: Brilliant nursing advice! Simple organizational tools like pill boxes, alarms, and visual charts can lift a huge weight off family caregivers and keep patients safe on their medication routine. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h7)

question: A patient wakes up restless, pacing, and yelling after getting a sedative. What is this unexpected reaction called?

options.A: Physical dependence
options.B: Drug tolerance
options.C: Paradoxical reaction
options.D: Allergic anaphylaxis

explanation: A paradoxical reaction is when a drug does the exact opposite of what you expect—making someone hyper instead of calm! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T2#GNS223_U6_T2_h7)

question: What does a U&E panel primarily assess in a patient?

options.A: Kidney function and electrolyte balance
options.B: Thyroid hormone production
options.C: Liver enzymes and clotting factors
options.D: Red and white blood cell counts

explanation: A U&E test specifically targets kidney health, hydration levels, and chemical minerals in the blood. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T9#GNS123_U2_T9_h1)

question: What are the three parts of the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Infection, immunity, and recovery
options.B: Source, symptom, and treatment
options.C: Vector, parasite, and climate
options.D: Agent, host, and environment

explanation: It's all about the agent causing the trouble, the host carrying it, and the environment bringing them together! [learn more](GNS313_U1_T10#GNS313_U1_T10_h2)

question: Why is postpartum hemorrhage a huge risk after a mother delivers twins?

options.A: The overstretched uterus contracts poorly after birth.
options.B: The placenta is always retained inside the fallopian tubes.
options.C: The mother has too much iron in her bloodstream.
options.D: Blood clotting factors completely disappear during labor.

explanation: Brilliant reasoning! Carrying multiples stretches the uterine muscles a lot. Afterward, it sometimes struggles to clamp back down firmly (we call this uterine atony), making bleeding a major risk to watch for. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T018#GNS226_U2_T018_h4)

question: Which of the following is a key component of a healthful school physical environment?

options.A: Private lockers for all enrolled students
options.B: Multi-story concrete laboratory blocks
options.C: Air conditioning in every single room
options.D: Clean and functional toilet facilities

explanation: Adequate sanitation and clean toilets are non-negotiable requirements for preventing disease transmission in schools. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h5)

question: How does general inflation negatively affect a Drug Revolving Fund over time?

options.A: It causes all tablets inside the store to dissolve faster
options.B: It increases the number of qualified pharmacists available
options.C: It prevents patients from visiting the hospital entirely
options.D: It reduces the purchasing power of the fund over time

explanation: When prices go up everywhere, the cash you have buys fewer replacement drugs than it used to. That's the challenge of inflation! [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h7)

question: A woman with sickle cell disease is admitted in active labor. What is the most critical nursing action for her care?

options.A: Restricting oral fluid intake to prevent swelling
options.B: Encouraging unmedicated natural childbirth at home
options.C: Maintaining strict intravenous hydration
options.D: Keeping the room temperature cold to prevent shivering

explanation: Spot on! Dehydration makes the blood thicker and can easily trigger a crisis, so keeping fluids flowing through an IV is an absolute must. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h5)

question: Why must a mother with mastitis keep removing milk from the infected breast?

options.A: Pumping removes the need to take prescribed antibiotics
options.B: Stopping milk removal cures the infection faster
options.C: Continued drainage prevents further milk stasis and reduces infection severity
options.D: It prevents the baby from getting any nutrition

explanation: Emptying the breast stops milk from sitting stagnant, which is what bacteria love. Keeping it flowing helps her heal faster! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h5)

question: What is a poultice primarily made of?

options.A: A dry powder swallowed with plenty of water
options.B: A clear liquid injected directly into a vein
options.C: A soft, moist mass spread on a cloth
options.D: A hard plastic shell strapped onto a broken bone

explanation: A poultice consists of a moist, soft mixture applied externally using a piece of cloth or gauze. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h1)

question: If a trauma patient's Glasgow Coma Scale score starts dropping over a couple of hours, what is the most likely reason?

options.A: Successful recovery from the primary injury
options.B: An allergic reaction to pain medication
options.C: Worsening intracranial pressure or bleeding
options.D: The normal healing process beginning

explanation: Spot on! A falling GCS score is a major warning sign that swelling or bleeding inside the head is getting worse and pressing on the brain. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T13#GNS222_U3_T13_h4)

question: Which of these conditions is a direct result of the gut failing to absorb nutrients over a long period?

options.A: Sudden high blood pressure
options.B: Iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: Acute kidney stone formation
options.D: Excessive red blood cell counts

explanation: Spot on! If a damaged gut lining can't absorb key minerals like iron, the body simply can't manufacture enough healthy red blood cells. Keep up the fantastic work! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h5)

question: Why are menstrual cycles often irregular during the first year or two after a girl's first period?

options.A: The thyroid gland temporarily stops working during adolescence
options.B: The uterus is still too small to hold a normal volume of blood
options.C: The cycles are frequently anovulatory as the endocrine system matures
options.D: Girls consume too much dietary iron during their growth spurts

explanation: You're getting the hang of this! Because ovulation doesn't happen every single month right away, it takes time for the hormonal system to settle into a steady rhythm. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which common group of over-the-counter pain relievers is a major cause of peptic ulcers?

options.A: Broad-spectrum oral antifungal agents
options.B: First-generation antihistamine pills
options.C: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
options.D: Fat-soluble multivitamin supplements

explanation: NSAIDs like ibuprofen block protective chemicals in the stomach lining, making it super easy for acid to cause damage. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h7)

question: When designing public health education, what does 'acceptability' mean?

options.A: Whether the target community welcomes and relates to the educational tool
options.B: Whether the government health ministry has stamped it with an official seal
options.C: How many pages of text the target population is willing to read
options.D: How cheaply the printing press can manufacture the paper flyers

explanation: Acceptability is all about whether the community feels comfortable with the material and feels it matches their personal values and beliefs. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h2)

question: When should a patient with chronic pancreatitis take their prescribed pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy?

options.A: With every meal and snack
options.B: Only when eating foods high in sugar
options.C: Only when abdominal pain begins
options.D: Once daily right before bedtime

explanation: Spot on! Enzymes need to be taken right along with all food and snacks so they can mix with the nutrients and help the body digest food properly. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h6)

question: What structure chemically connects the hypothalamus to the anterior pituitary gland?

options.A: A specialized portal blood vessel system
options.B: Direct lymphatic drainage channels
options.C: The cerebrospinal fluid ventricles
options.D: Direct unmyelinated nerve fiber tracks

explanation: The hypothalamus uses a dedicated mini-blood highway (a portal system) to send chemical messenger hormones straight to the anterior pituitary. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T1#GNS222_U2_T1_h6)

question: Which physical sign should a nurse look for when monitoring a patient for worsening heart failure due to severe CAD?

options.A: Swelling in the lower legs and ankles
options.B: Bleeding gums when brushing the teeth
options.C: Sudden uncontrollable muscle twitching
options.D: Yellow discoloration of the eye whites

explanation: When a damaged heart pumps inefficiently, fluid backs up in the body, commonly causing dependent edema in the legs and ankles. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h8)

question: Roughly what percentage of all waste generated in a healthcare facility is non-hazardous general waste?
explanation: You'd be surprised! The vast majority of hospital waste (around 75% to 90%) is actually regular, non-hazardous stuff from everyday operations, just like household trash. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h1)

question: Which patient position is best for chest tube insertion to help expand the lung and make the area easy to reach?

options.A: Left lateral decubitus position only
options.B: Semi-Fowler's or high-Fowler's position
options.C: Trendelenburg position with feet elevated

question: What is the most accurate way for a nurse to monitor daily changes in a patient's fluid balance?

options.A: Taking daily body weights
options.B: Measuring abdominal girth
options.C: Checking skin turgor every morning
options.D: Counting the number of wet diapers or pads

explanation: Daily weight measurement is the gold standard because rapid weight changes directly reflect gain or loss of body water. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h7)

question: Why do some clients stop seeing their period (amenorrhea) while using progestin-only injections?

options.A: Thickening of the blood inside the uterus
options.B: Permanent damage to the ovaries
options.C: Complete blockage of the cervical canal
options.D: Thinning and resting of the uterine lining

explanation: No regular estrogen means the uterine lining stays thin and relaxed, so there's barely any tissue to shed during a monthly period. Totally normal! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h5)

question: Which sense is widely believed to be the last to fade as a patient approaches death?

options.A: Taste
options.B: Hearing
options.C: Sight
options.D: Smell

explanation: Even when a dying patient appears unresponsive, their hearing often remains intact, which is why nurses advise families to keep talking to them. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T12#GNS321_U4_T12_h2)

question: Which chemical messenger (neurotransmitter) is mainly responsible for making the detrusor muscle contract during urination?

options.A: Norepinephrine
options.B: Serotonin
options.C: Acetylcholine
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: Acetylcholine is the key player here! It binds to receptors on the bladder wall to trigger that squeezing action. You're doing great. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h4)

question: How does your nervous system's 'fight-or-flight' (sympathetic) response affect your intestines?

options.A: It widens the intestinal lumen
options.B: It stimulates rapid peristaltic waves
options.C: It increases digestive enzyme output
options.D: It decreases motility and secretion

explanation: When you're stressed or running from danger, your body shuts down non-essentials like digestion to focus energy on surviving. Rest and digest takes a back seat! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h7)

question: Which dangerous infections can spread when unsterile syringes are reused?

options.A: Hypertension and diabetes
options.B: Hepatitis and HIV
options.C: Malaria and typhoid
options.D: Asthma and bronchitis

explanation: Correct! Reusing syringes is a major way bloodborne infections like HIV and hepatitis spread globally. Safety first, always! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h3)

question: In public health, what does immunization coverage tell us?

options.A: The number of health workers trained in vaccine administration
options.B: The proportion of people who received recommended vaccines
options.C: The financial cost of running vaccination campaigns
options.D: The total number of vaccines stored in national warehouses

explanation: You've got this! Immunization coverage simply tracks the percentage of the target population that successfully got their scheduled doses. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T69#GNS214_U1_T69_h1)

question: How can public health nurses use incidence data to check if an immunization campaign worked?

options.A: By calculating the average age of patients in the ward
options.B: By measuring the total money spent on medical supplies
options.C: By checking if the number of new infections drops over time
options.D: By counting the total number of hospital beds available

explanation: If a vaccination drive is successful, you should see the number of new infections (incidence) go way down. Awesome nursing logic! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h6)

question: Why is the abbreviation 'u' for units placed on safety watch lists?

options.A: It stands for an entirely different drug name in the pharmacy
options.B: It only applies to liquid medications given through feeding tubes
options.C: It is too long to write quickly during a busy hospital shift
options.D: It is easily mistaken for a zero or four, causing massive overdoses

explanation: That's right! A handwritten 'u' can easily look like a '0' or a '4', leading to dangerous dosing mistakes (like reading 4 units as 40 units!). That's why safety committees flag it. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T8#GNS125_U2_T8_h5)

question: Which major blood vessel feeds oxygen-rich blood to the small intestine and the first part of the large intestine?

options.A: Superior mesenteric artery
options.B: Celiac trunk
options.C: Inferior mesenteric artery
options.D: Renal artery

explanation: The superior mesenteric artery is the main lifeline branching off the aorta to supply the small intestine and upper colon. Keep crushing it! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h7)

question: Which action best demonstrates effective psychosocial support by the nurse for a dying patient?

options.A: Leaving the room immediately when the patient starts crying
options.B: Telling the patient not to worry about the future
options.C: Sitting quietly by the bed and listening attentively to their concerns
options.D: Insisting that family members leave so the patient can rest

explanation: Active listening and quiet presence validate the patient's feelings and provide deep emotional comfort during a vulnerable time. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T12#GNS321_U4_T12_h4)

question: What are the classic signs that a patient has developed a post-abortion pelvic infection?

options.A: Foul-smelling vaginal discharge and fever
options.B: Clear, watery discharge lasting several days
options.C: Sudden painless swelling of the lower limbs
options.D: High blood pressure and severe throbbing headache

explanation: Spot on! Bad-smelling discharge and fever are major warning signs that bacteria have entered the uterus. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h5)

question: During a pelvic exam, what specific finding strongly points toward a condition like salpingitis?

options.A: Hyperactive bowel sounds in all four quadrants
options.B: Complete absence of deep tendon reflexes
options.C: Cervical motion tenderness
options.D: Painless enlargement of the spleen

explanation: Cervical motion tenderness happens when moving the cervix causes sudden, sharp pain because the inflamed pelvic organs right above it are disturbed. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h5)
